input.description: Design community roster + Authentik
input.prompt:
Write a design doc for GitHub issue #166 (read it: `gh issue view 166`). It covers a community roster in the portal, with Authentik as the community identity provider. Work in the worktree /Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/community-roster.

The user wants: "a team + school roster for participants in race team. At the program level (e.g. Double-handed), not the J-Pod level. Guardians and participants should be able to login and see their data and contact info of other people on their team." They don't want families to have to create and manage another account if possible.

Decisions already made by the user (do not relitigate; they are in the issue body):
- Authentik is the single identity provider. Sign in with Google is the main path, and an emailed one-time code or link is the fallback. Directus and the portal trust Authentik over OIDC. Authentik's proxy outpost replaces oauth2-proxy as Caddy's forward_auth gate (packages/substrate/deploy/Caddyfile, docker-compose.yml).
- Codes are emailed via the Google Workspace SMTP relay for now; SES (#71) later.
- The UI is an extension of the portal (packages/portal), which is meant for the whole CYC community. Today it's a static page gated to all@ (#82, #98).
- Authorization is split. Authentik groups decide which portal sections someone sees; a sync job writes those groups from CRM roles, following gsuite-sync's plan-and-execute shape (#156). Directus permission rules (packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts, see guardianFilter) decide which rows someone can read. The portal makes no data-access decisions.
- Guardians and all participants can log in. A minor's own contact info is never shown to others.
- Read-only, except each family's own opt-in toggle.
- Opt-in is per family and lasts until withdrawn. Families opt in from the portal now. From Spring, a Clubspot custom field also collects it at registration and reaches a people column through promoted_fields. The design must say how the app toggle and the synced Clubspot value coexist (see #137).
- Names are always visible to teammates. For opted-in families, each guardian's name, email, and phone appear (all guardians Clubspot lists).
- Scope: every program, current season. A roster is per program (programs, via classes.program_id), listing participants with a confirmed registration_entries row, each with their school. Filters for team (the class within the program, e.g. J-Pod/K-Pod/L-Pod) and school. people.school is free text from Clubspot, so address normalization.
- FreeScout could later use Authentik via its SAML module; out of scope here beyond not precluding it.

Things the design should investigate and propose (call out any that are genuinely the user's decision as open questions):
- The order of work. For example, moving the existing portal and staff onto Authentik with no behavior change first, then adding families.
- Where staff and volunteer groups come from (Google Groups all@ vs CRM).
- VM memory headroom for Authentik (packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/compute.ts) and its Postgres on the existing Cloud SQL instance.
- How Authentik config stays in the repo (blueprints vs a Pulumi provider), consistent with the Pulumi class-based pattern.
- Hostnames, and whether Directus shares a parent domain with the portal so its session or cookie works for the portal's API calls. Otherwise, what the token handoff looks like.
- Linking a login to people rows: one email maps to several people (a parent and a child sharing an email), emails change, and an email with no match must fail closed.
- How the Directus user gets linked to people.directus_user_id (packages/directus schema), and the Directus roles/policies for guardian and participant.
- The roster read permission, expressed as Directus filters, including hiding minors' contact info and non-opted-in guardians' contact info. Can Directus field-level permissions do this, or does it need a separate view or collection?
- The portal's shape: static page plus client JS calling Directus, and how sections are gated by group.
- The email sender identity, and SPF/DKIM for the relay.

Keep the doc short, and follow the repo's prose rules. Return the doc path, a short summary, and your open questions. Only include questions that are real decisions for the user.

entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

  I wrote the design doc for #166. I didn't commit it, and I changed no source files.
  
  **Doc:** /Users/ungood/workspaces/personal/isthmia/.claude/worktrees/community-roster/.claude/plans/community-roster.md
  
  **Summary**
  1. Families get their own Authentik-gated site, proposed as `my.cycsail.team`, with Authentik at `login.cycsail.team`. `cycsail.team` stays on oauth2-proxy and `all@`, and Directus staff keep the `google` provider. Signing in to Authentik grants no data. Caddy serves a roster page to members of the Authentik group `community-families` and a help page to everyone else. Both pages carry the public links.
  2. A new `community-sync` Cloud Run job, built plan-and-execute like gsuite-sync, rebuilds four collections every run. `community_logins` maps a normalized email to the participants that login acts for, which handles a shared family email. The others are `rosters`, `roster_entries` and `roster_contacts`. It never writes a minor's own contact info, and an unknown date of birth counts as a minor. The same job manages the Authentik users and the `community-families` group.
  3. Directus gets one new Community role. It is the `authentik` provider's default role, with public registration on. Every rule is keyed on `$CURRENT_USER.email` through `community_logins`, so an email with no match reads nothing. Contact visibility is a live rule on `participant_id.share_contact`, so opting in or withdrawing takes effect at once. `share_contact` is a nullable boolean on the participant's `people` row. The portal toggle wins over the Clubspot value, which only fills in a family that never answered, because `promoted_fields` fills gaps only.
  
  **Things you should know**
  - **Email deliverability is broken today, independent of this work.** `cyccommunitysailing.org` publishes two SPF records, one for Google and one for Amazon SES. Two records are an SPF permerror, so receivers treat all mail from the domain as unauthenticated. There is also no DKIM key at the default `google._domainkey` selector. That DNS lives at the registrar, not in Cloud DNS, so the fix is a manual step (it's in the doc). The login codes will go to spam until it's done.
  - `dev/directus-local` runs without a license, so the Directus permission rules can't be tested locally. The doc verifies them in production with two test families in Clubspot, before board approval opens the site.
  - I answered the `people.directus_user_id` question by not using it for families. That column is unique, so it can't map one shared email to several people, and linking through it would need near-admin rights on `directus_users`.
  - Board/safeguarding approval is listed as a launch prerequisite, not a build blocker. Moving staff onto Authentik and retiring oauth2-proxy are listed as future work only.
  
  **Open questions for the user**
  1. **Community hostname.** Is `my.cycsail.team` the right name? Families will see it in every message.
  2. **Team membership is computed by the job, not by Directus filters.** Doing it with filters alone would span about nine relations and could only be checked on a live licensed instance. Contact visibility stays a live Directus rule. This departs from "Directus rules decide rows" for team membership only. Accept it?
  3. **Current season.** Proposed: camps running today, else the next upcoming camp, else the most recently ended one. Is that right between seasons, and while Spring registration is open during Fall?
  4. **Clubspot versus the portal.** Proposed: the portal choice wins permanently. A family that answers "No" on a new Clubspot form after choosing "Yes" in the portal stays shared until they change it in the portal. Accept that, or let the newer answer win?
  5. **Adults and minors.** Proposed: an adult participant's own contact info appears if they opt in, and a minor's own login cannot change the family toggle. Confirm both?
  6. **VM resize.** Authentik wants about 2 GB, and the VM is an `e2-medium` with 4 GB that already runs Directus, Caddy and oauth2-proxy. Moving to `e2-standard-2` costs about $25 a month more. May the implementer resize if measurement shows less than 1 GB free?
  7. **Addresses.** Which address sends the login codes, and which contact should the help page give?
</agent-message>

260 .claude/plans/community-roster.md
# Community roster on Authentik

## Context

Race team families cannot find the other people on their team (#166). The CRM already holds the
data, but no family can log in, and no permission rule lets anyone read another family's rows.

- Every request to `cycsail.team` goes through oauth2-proxy, and only `all@` members pass
  (`packages/substrate/deploy/Caddyfile:18-43`, `docker-compose.yml:38`). Families are not in
  `all@`, so they cannot reach the site.
- The Guardian policy lets a guardian read only their own minors (`guardianFilter`,
  `packages/infrastructure/src/crm/index.ts:93-113`). The Guardian role has no login
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/directus-roles.ts:42-56`).
- `people.directus_user_id` is unique (`packages/directus/schema.yaml:943`). A family commonly
  shares one email across a parent and a child, so one login cannot map to one person.
- `people` has no minor flag. `date_of_birth` is nullable (`packages/crm/src/people.ts:7`).
- gsuite-sync already computes "confirmed participants of a program, plus their guardians"
  (`packages/gsuite-sync/src/membership.ts:58-110`). Its 12-month camp window
  (`packages/gsuite-sync/src/camps.ts:8`) would merge last Spring's team into this Fall's roster.

**Email deliverability is broken today.** `cyccommunitysailing.org` publishes two SPF records
(`include:_spf.google.com` and `include:amazonses.com`). Two records are an SPF permerror, so
receivers treat all mail from the domain as unauthenticated. No DKIM key exists at the default
`google._domainkey` selector. The domain's DNS is at the registrar, not in the Cloud DNS zone
(`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/dns.ts:191` is inert). Login codes will land in spam
until this is fixed.

## Approach

Families come first. Staff stay on oauth2-proxy and `all@`, unchanged.

### Hostnames and gating

- `login.cycsail.team` — Authentik.
- `my.cycsail.team` (name to confirm) — the community site, gated by Authentik's embedded proxy
  outpost through Caddy `forward_auth`. The gate admits any signed-in Authentik user.
- `cycsail.team` — the staff portal. It stays on oauth2-proxy with no change.
- `directus.cycsail.team` — unchanged host. It gains an `authentik` auth provider next to `google`.

A separate hostname keeps one gate per Caddy site block. A path split on `cycsail.team` puts two
gates and two session cookies on one host, and `/` would still reject families.

Anyone who can prove an email can sign in, through Google or an emailed code. Signing in grants no
data. The public links on the community site must hold nothing sensitive.

### Who is on a team: `community-sync`

A new package and Cloud Run job, `packages/community-sync`, with the plan-and-execute shape of
gsuite-sync. It depends on `commodore`, `directus`, `crm`, and `clubspot`. It does not invert the
graph. Its `schema.yaml` owns four collections:

- `community_logins` — `email` (normalized), `person_id`, `relationship` (`self` or `guardian`).
  One row per participant a login acts for. A participant's own valid email gives a `self` row.
  Each guardian's valid email gives a `guardian` row. A shared email gets several rows. An email
  with no row gets nothing.
- `rosters` — one per program, for the current season.
- `roster_entries` — participant name, team (class name), school, and `participant_id`.
- `roster_contacts` — one row per guardian of each roster participant: name, email, phone, and
  `participant_id`. An adult participant (date of birth known, 18 or older) also gets a `self` row.
  **A minor's own contact is never written.** Unknown date of birth counts as a minor.

The job rebuilds all four on every run and deletes stale rows. This differs from gsuite-sync, which
is add-only (`membership.ts:121-124`). A stale row here is access that should be gone.

"Current season", per program: camps running today. If none are running, the next upcoming camp.
If none are upcoming, the most recently ended camp. Entries count when `status` is `confirmed`.

School filtering uses a key from `normalizeName` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:11`).
Spelling variants beyond case and punctuation are fixed by staff editing `people.school`.

Move `normalizeEmail` and `isValidEmail` (`membership.ts:34-45`) into `crm`, so both syncs share
one rule for what counts as a login email.

### Contact opt-in: `people.share_contact`

A nullable boolean on `people`, declared in `crm`. It is set on the **participant** row, because
Spring's Clubspot custom field reaches `people` through `promoted_fields`, which writes the
registration's person. Null means "never answered", and it is treated as not shared.

- The portal's one family toggle writes `true` or `false` to every participant the viewer acts for
  as a guardian. A minor's `self` login gets no toggle.
- From Spring, `promoted_fields` gap-fills the column (`packages/clubspot/src/promoted-fields.ts:7`).
  Clubspot then seeds only a family that has never answered. After a portal choice, a later
  Clubspot answer is ignored. That makes the portal the one place to withdraw.
- `PROMOTABLE_PERSON_FIELDS` allows text columns only. Spring needs an explicit Yes/No parse that
  counts and logs any other answer, and never defaults it.
- If #137 replaces gap-fill with a three-way merge, `share_contact` must stay portal-owned.

### Directus permissions

One new role, **Community**, with `appAccess: false`. It is the `authentik` provider's
`DEFAULT_ROLE_ID`, with public registration on. That is safe because every Community rule is keyed
on `$CURRENT_USER.email` through `community_logins`. A user with no rows reads nothing. The sync
writes no `directus_users` rows and needs no rights on them.

- `rosters`, `roster_entries`: read where the roster's program has an entry whose participant has
  a `community_logins` row with the viewer's email.
- `roster_contacts`: the same filter, **and** `participant_id.share_contact = true`. This is a live
  rule, so an opt-in or a withdrawal takes effect at once, not on the next run.
- `people`: read and update, `fields: [id, first_name, last_name, share_contact]`, where a
  `guardian` row in `community_logins` has the viewer's email. That is enough to render the toggle.
- Never `medical_profiles`, `contacts`, or `registrations`.

Staff keep `google`, and `people.directus_user_id` stays staff-only. The Guardian role stays
unused.

Two settings keep `$CURRENT_USER.email` trustworthy:

- Authentik must not let users change their own email.
- Directus keeps `AUTH_AUTHENTIK_SYNC_USER_INFO` off, so the email is set once, at registration.

### Portal: `packages/portal`

The portal builds a second static site next to today's page. Today's page does not change.

- Caddy strips any client-sent `X-Authentik-Groups` header, then runs `forward_auth`. It serves the
  roster page to members of the `community-families` group and the help page to everyone else.
  Both pages carry the public links section. This is #98's per-audience page option, with two
  audiences.
- The roster page uses plain ESM from `tsc` with no bundler. It calls `directus.cycsail.team` with
  `credentials: "include"`. No token reaches JavaScript.
- Directus keeps its host-only session cookie. `my.` and `directus.` are the same site, so the
  `Lax` cookie goes with the request. Directus needs `CORS_ORIGIN=https://my.cycsail.team`,
  `CORS_CREDENTIALS=true`, and the community URL in `AUTH_AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_ALLOW_LIST`. A
  parent-domain cookie was rejected because every future subdomain would receive it.
- The help page says to use the email the family registered with in Clubspot, or to contact us.
- Filtering by team and school, and rendering, are pure functions tested like
  `packages/portal/test/render.test.ts`.

### Authentik groups

`community-sync`'s groups pass makes one Authentik user per distinct `community_logins` email, if
none exists. It then reconciles `community-families` membership, with adds and removes. Users are
created ahead of time, so the group is in place at a family's first sign-in. The Google source
uses email matching to link a new Google login to that user. The pass writes through an interface
that tests mock, as gsuite-sync's `MemberAdder` does.

The Authentik token for the sync belongs to a service account. Its RBAC role can create users and
change membership of the managed group only. Staff and volunteer groups do not come from this job.
They stay on `all@` until the staff migration.

### Authentik deployment

- **Containers.** `authentik-server` and `authentik-worker` in
  `packages/substrate/deploy/docker-compose.yml`, plus Caddy blocks for `login.` and `my.`. Pin a
  release that needs no Redis.
- **Database.** `postgres.database("authentik")` and a user on the existing instance
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/database.ts:122-141`). `db-g1-small` allows about
  50 connections. Cap Authentik's workers and connection age so that it and Directus fit.
- **Memory.** Authentik wants about 2 GB. The VM is `e2-medium` with 4 GB (`compute.ts:11`), and it
  already runs Directus, Caddy, and oauth2-proxy. Measure `docker stats` before the first step
  ships. Resize to `e2-standard-2` if less than 1 GB stays free. `allowStoppingForUpdate` makes that
  a reboot (`compute.ts:61`).
- **Secrets.** Pulumi generates the bootstrap token, the secret key, the DB password, and the
  Directus OIDC client secret with `randomSecret` in `infrastructure`, and grants them to
  `substrate-runner`.
- **Config.** A new Pulumi project, `packages/infrastructure/src/authentik`, applied after
  `infrastructure`. It uses the goauthentik Terraform provider through
  `pulumi package add terraform-provider`, wrapped in classes with secure defaults. It declares the
  Google source, the email-code flow, SMTP, the `my.` proxy application, the Directus OIDC
  application, the managed group, and the sync's service account. It reads the Directus client
  secret by name, the way `crm/index.ts:37-41` reads the admin password. That avoids a cycle
  between the two projects.
- **IAM.** The job's service account goes in `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap`, like
  `gsuite-sync.ts`. Its grants go in `packages/infrastructure/src/config.ts`. Its Directus machine
  user gets read on `people`, `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `classes`,
  `camps`, and `programs`, and full access to its own four collections. Its `people` access is
  read-only. Portal users write `share_contact`, not the sync.

### Email

Authentik sends through the Workspace SMTP relay. The relay authenticates the VM's static IP
(`compute.ts:24`) and allows only addresses in the domain. Before launch, fix DNS at the registrar:

1. Merge the two SPF records into one:
   `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all`.
2. Turn on Workspace DKIM, and publish its key.
3. Delete the stray `v=DMARC1` TXT record at the apex. `_dmarc` already holds the real one.

### Testing

Unit tests cover the plan functions: logins, the season choice, rosters, the minor-contact
exclusion, and the group diff. They also cover the portal's filters and rendering. The Directus
rules are license-gated, and `dev/directus-local` runs without a license
(`dev/directus-local/docker-compose.yml:10`). Verify them in production with two test families in
Clubspot:

- one opted in, one not
- one sharing an email between a parent and a child

Check what each login reads through the REST API. Authentik config is checked with `pulumi preview`
and a sign-in through each path.

### Launch prerequisite

Do not open `my.cycsail.team` to families before the board approves sharing names and contact
information. Build and verify with test accounts before that approval.

### Future work

Move staff onto Authentik. Sync `all@` or #156's role model into Authentik groups, switch
Directus staff to the `authentik` provider, and retire oauth2-proxy. FreeScout can join later
through Authentik's SAML module.

## Alternatives

- **Path-based gates on `cycsail.team`.** Two gates in one site block, and families could not use
  `/`. Rejected for a separate hostname.
- **The roster as pure Directus filters on `people`.** The teammate test spans about nine
  relations. It needs new aliases on `programs` and `classes`, and it repeats gsuite-sync's rules in
  JSON that only a live licensed instance can check. Directus 11+ can scope fields per policy, so
  names-versus-contact is expressible. Membership is not practical. The contact gate stays live.
- **Link logins through `people.directus_user_id`.** It is unique, so a shared family email cannot
  map to several people. It also needs the sync to create `directus_users` rows, which is near-admin
  access.
- **Authentik blueprints.** Files would have to reach the VM beside the compose file. Removing an
  entry does not delete the object, and there is no preview.
- **Client-side section filtering from a `/whoami` endpoint.** It needs JSON templated from a
  header. The Caddy page choice has no templating.

## Open questions

1. **Community hostname.** `my.cycsail.team` is proposed. Families will see this name in every
   message.
2. **Materialized team membership.** Who is on a team is computed by `community-sync`, not written
   as Directus filters. The contact gate is still a live Directus rule. This departs from "Directus
   rules decide rows" for membership only. Accept it?
3. **Current season.** Proposed: camps running today, else the next upcoming camp, else the most
   recently ended camp. Is that the right roster between seasons, and while Spring registration
   is open during Fall?
4. **Clubspot versus the portal.** Proposed: the portal choice wins, and a later Clubspot answer
   never overrides it. A family that says "No" on a new Clubspot form after a portal "Yes" stays
   shared until they change it in the portal. Accept, or let the newer answer win?
5. **Adult participants and minors.** Proposed: an adult participant's own contact appears if they
   opt in. A minor's `self` login cannot change the family toggle. Confirm both.
6. **VM resize.** Resizing to `e2-standard-2` costs about $25 a month more. May the implementer
   resize if measurement shows less than 1 GB free?
7. **Addresses.** Which address sends the login codes, and which contact does the help page give?

## Steps

1. `crm`: add `people.share_contact`, and move `normalizeEmail` and `isValidEmail` from
   gsuite-sync. Schema change, serialized.
2. `community-sync`: the schema for the four collections, and the plan functions with tests.
   Serialized with step 1's schema.
3. `community-sync`: the executor, Dockerfile, Cloud Run job, bootstrap identity, IAM, Directus
   machine user, and permission rules. Deploy it, then check rosters in the Data Studio before any
   family can log in.
4. Infrastructure: measure memory, resize if approved, then add the Authentik database, secrets,
   containers, the `login.` DNS record, and its Caddy block.
5. The `authentik` Pulumi project: Google source, email flow, SMTP, applications, group, and the
   sync's service account. Add it to `just deploy` and `docs/manual-setup.md`, including the relay
   and the DNS fixes.
6. Directus: the `authentik` provider, CORS, the Community role, and its permission rules.
7. `community-sync`: the Authentik groups pass.
8. Portal and substrate: the community site, the `my.` DNS record, and the Caddy block with the
   header strip and the group-based page choice.
9. Docs: READMEs, and the `CLAUDE.md` package list and graph.
10. Verify with the test families. Launch after board approval.
11. Spring: the Clubspot opt-in field as a `promoted_fields` target, with the Yes/No parse.

"Current season", per program: camps running today. If none are running, the next upcoming camp.
If none are upcoming, the most recently ended camp. Entries count when `status` is `confirmed`.

School filtering uses a key from `normalizeName` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:11`).
Spelling variants beyond case and punctuation are fixed by staff editing `people.school`.

Move `normalizeEmail` and `isValidEmail` (`membership.ts:34-45`) into `crm`, so both syncs share
one rule for what counts as a login email.

### Contact opt-in: `people.share_contact`

A nullable boolean on `people`, declared in `crm`. It is set on the **participant** row, because
Spring's Clubspot custom field reaches `people` through `promoted_fields`, which writes the
registration's person. Null means "never answered", and it is treated as not shared.

- The portal's one family toggle writes `true` or `false` to every participant the viewer acts for
  as a guardian. A minor's `self` login gets no toggle.
- From Spring, `promoted_fields` gap-fills the column (`packages/clubspot/src/promoted-fields.ts:7`).
  Clubspot then seeds only a family that has never answered. After a portal choice, a later
  Clubspot answer is ignored. That makes the portal the one place to withdraw.
- `PROMOTABLE_PERSON_FIELDS` allows text columns only. Spring needs an explicit Yes/No parse that
  counts and logs any other answer, and never defaults it.
- If #137 replaces gap-fill with a three-way merge, `share_contact` must stay portal-owned.

### Directus permissions

One new role, **Community**, with `appAccess: false`. It is the `authentik` provider's
`DEFAULT_ROLE_ID`, with public registration on. That is safe because every Community rule is keyed
on `$CURRENT_USER.email` through `community_logins`. A user with no rows reads nothing. The sync
writes no `directus_users` rows and needs no rights on them.

- `rosters`, `roster_entries`: read where the roster's program has an entry whose participant has
  a `community_logins` row with the viewer's email.
- `roster_contacts`: the same filter, **and** `participant_id.share_contact = true`. This is a live
  rule, so an opt-in or a withdrawal takes effect at once, not on the next run.
- `people`: read and update, `fields: [id, first_name, last_name, share_contact]`, where a
  `guardian` row in `community_logins` has the viewer's email. That is enough to render the toggle.
- Never `medical_profiles`, `contacts`, or `registrations`.

Staff keep `google`, and `people.directus_user_id` stays staff-only. The Guardian role stays
unused.

Two settings keep `$CURRENT_USER.email` trustworthy:

- Authentik must not let users change their own email.
- Directus keeps `AUTH_AUTHENTIK_SYNC_USER_INFO` off, so the email is set once, at registration.

### Portal: `packages/portal`

The portal builds a second static site next to today's page. Today's page does not change.

- Caddy strips any client-sent `X-Authentik-Groups` header, then runs `forward_auth`. It serves the
  roster page to members of the `community-families` group and the help page to everyone else.
  Both pages carry the public links section. This is #98's per-audience page option, with two
  audiences.
- The roster page uses plain ESM from `tsc` with no bundler. It calls `directus.cycsail.team` with
  `credentials: "include"`. No token reaches JavaScript.
- Directus keeps its host-only session cookie. `my.` and `directus.` are the same site, so the
  `Lax` cookie goes with the request. Directus needs `CORS_ORIGIN=https://my.cycsail.team`,
  `CORS_CREDENTIALS=true`, and the community URL in `AUTH_AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_ALLOW_LIST`. A
  parent-domain cookie was rejected because every future subdomain would receive it.
- The help page says to use the email the family registered with in Clubspot, or to contact us.
- Filtering by team and school, and rendering, are pure functions tested like
  `packages/portal/test/render.test.ts`.

### Authentik groups

`community-sync`'s groups pass makes one Authentik user per distinct `community_logins` email, if
none exists. It then reconciles `community-families` membership, with adds and removes. Users are
created ahead of time, so the group is in place at a family's first sign-in. The Google source
uses email matching to link a new Google login to that user. The pass writes through an interface
that tests mock, as gsuite-sync's `MemberAdder` does.

The Authentik token for the sync belongs to a service account. Its RBAC role can create users and
change membership of the managed group only. Staff and volunteer groups do not come from this job.
They stay on `all@` until the staff migration.

### Authentik deployment

- **Containers.** `authentik-server` and `authentik-worker` in
  `packages/substrate/deploy/docker-compose.yml`, plus Caddy blocks for `login.` and `my.`. Pin a
  release that needs no Redis.
- **Database.** `postgres.database("authentik")` and a user on the existing instance
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/database.ts:122-141`). `db-g1-small` allows about
  50 connections. Cap Authentik's workers and connection age so that it and Directus fit.
- **Memory.** Authentik wants about 2 GB. The VM is `e2-medium` with 4 GB (`compute.ts:11`), and it
  already runs Directus, Caddy, and oauth2-proxy. Measure `docker stats` before the first step
  ships. Resize to `e2-standard-2` if less than 1 GB stays free. `allowStoppingForUpdate` makes that
  a reboot (`compute.ts:61`).
- **Secrets.** Pulumi generates the bootstrap token, the secret key, the DB password, and the
  Directus OIDC client secret with `randomSecret` in `infrastructure`, and grants them to
  `substrate-runner`.
- **Config.** A new Pulumi project, `packages/infrastructure/src/authentik`, applied after
  `infrastructure`. It uses the goauthentik Terraform provider through
  `pulumi package add terraform-provider`, wrapped in classes with secure defaults. It declares the
  Google source, the email-code flow, SMTP, the `my.` proxy application, the Directus OIDC
  application, the managed group, and the sync's service account. It reads the Directus client
  secret by name, the way `crm/index.ts:37-41` reads the admin password. That avoids a cycle
  between the two projects.
- **IAM.** The job's service account goes in `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap`, like
  `gsuite-sync.ts`. Its grants go in `packages/infrastructure/src/config.ts`. Its Directus machine
  user gets read on `people`, `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `classes`,
  `camps`, and `programs`, and full access to its own four collections. Its `people` access is
  read-only. Portal users write `share_contact`, not the sync.

### Email

Authentik sends through the Workspace SMTP relay. The relay authenticates the VM's static IP
(`compute.ts:24`) and allows only addresses in the domain. Before launch, fix DNS at the registrar:

1. Merge the two SPF records into one:
   `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all`.
2. Turn on Workspace DKIM, and publish its key.
3. Delete the stray `v=DMARC1` TXT record at the apex. `_dmarc` already holds the real one.

### Testing

Unit tests cover the plan functions: logins, the season choice, rosters, the minor-contact
exclusion, and the group diff. They also cover the portal's filters and rendering. The Directus
rules are license-gated, and `dev/directus-local` runs without a license
(`dev/directus-local/docker-compose.yml:10`). Verify them in production with two test families in
Clubspot:

- one opted in, one not
- one sharing an email between a parent and a child

Check what each login reads through the REST API. Authentik config is checked with `pulumi preview`
and a sign-in through each path.

### Launch prerequisite

Do not open `my.cycsail.team` to families before the board approves sharing names and contact
information. Build and verify with test accounts before that approval.

### Future work

Move staff onto Authentik. Sync `all@` or #156's role model into Authentik groups, switch
Directus staff to the `authentik` provider, and retire oauth2-proxy. FreeScout can join later
through Authentik's SAML module.

## Alternatives

- **Path-based gates on `cycsail.team`.** Two gates in one site block, and families could not use
  `/`. Rejected for a separate hostname.
- **The roster as pure Directus filters on `people`.** The teammate test spans about nine
  relations. It needs new aliases on `programs` and `classes`, and it repeats gsuite-sync's rules in
  JSON that only a live licensed instance can check. Directus 11+ can scope fields per policy, so
  names-versus-contact is expressible. Membership is not practical. The contact gate stays live.
- **Link logins through `people.directus_user_id`.** It is unique, so a shared family email cannot
  map to several people. It also needs the sync to create `directus_users` rows, which is near-admin
  access.
- **Authentik blueprints.** Files would have to reach the VM beside the compose file. Removing an
  entry does not delete the object, and there is no preview.
- **Client-side section filtering from a `/whoami` endpoint.** It needs JSON templated from a
  header. The Caddy page choice has no templating.

## Open questions

1. **Community hostname.** `my.cycsail.team` is proposed. Families will see this name in every
   message.
2. **Materialized team membership.** Who is on a team is computed by `community-sync`, not written
   as Directus filters. The contact gate is still a live Directus rule. This departs from "Directus
   rules decide rows" for membership only. Accept it?
3. **Current season.** Proposed: camps running today, else the next upcoming camp, else the most
   recently ended camp. Is that the right roster between seasons, and while Spring registration
   is open during Fall?
4. **Clubspot versus the portal.** Proposed: the portal choice wins, and a later Clubspot answer
   never overrides it. A family that says "No" on a new Clubspot form after a portal "Yes" stays
   shared until they change it in the portal. Accept, or let the newer answer win?
5. **Adult participants and minors.** Proposed: an adult participant's own contact appears if they
   opt in. A minor's `self` login cannot change the family toggle. Confirm both.
6. **VM resize.** Resizing to `e2-standard-2` costs about $25 a month more. May the implementer
   resize if measurement shows less than 1 GB free?
7. **Addresses.** Which address sends the login codes, and which contact does the help page give?

## Steps

1. `crm`: add `people.share_contact`, and move `normalizeEmail` and `isValidEmail` from
   gsuite-sync. Schema change, serialized.
2. `community-sync`: the schema for the four collections, and the plan functions with tests.
   Serialized with step 1's schema.
3. `community-sync`: the executor, Dockerfile, Cloud Run job, bootstrap identity, IAM, Directus
   machine user, and permission rules. Deploy it, then check rosters in the Data Studio before any
   family can log in.
4. Infrastructure: measure memory, resize if approved, then add the Authentik database, secrets,
   containers, the `login.` DNS record, and its Caddy block.
5. The `authentik` Pulumi project: Google source, email flow, SMTP, applications, group, and the
   sync's service account. Add it to `just deploy` and `docs/manual-setup.md`, including the relay
   and the DNS fixes.
6. Directus: the `authentik` provider, CORS, the Community role, and its permission rules.
7. `community-sync`: the Authentik groups pass.
8. Portal and substrate: the community site, the `my.` DNS record, and the Caddy block with the
   header strip and the group-based page choice.
9. Docs: READMEs, and the `CLAUDE.md` package list and graph.
10. Verify with the test families. Launch after board approval.
11. Spring: the Clubspot opt-in field as a `promoted_fields` target, with the Yes/No parse.

Decisions locked (2026-08-02) for the isthmia self-hosted platform foundation, epic #64 (Phase 0 of `docs/architecture.md`). Plan approved via `plan-review` label removal.

- **Compute shape: single Compute Engine VM on Container-Optimized OS (COS), Tier B.** Apps run as containers behind Caddy + oauth2-proxy on one VM (e2-medium 4GB floor, resize to e2-standard-2 8GB when tight). Clubspot sync stays a Cloud Run Job. GKE is out. **Chose COS over NixOS** (decided #86, slice 5): workload is entirely containers, so COS (Google-maintained, auto-patching, minimal) beats NixOS, which would add an image-build pipeline for host features the workload doesn't use. Compose stack + config in git; VM disposable.
- **Databases on managed Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL** (`db-g1-small` shared-core, ~$29/mo) — Directus, Listmonk, **and FreeScout** all on Postgres (user confirmed FreeScout supports Postgres, so no separate MariaDB/MySQL). Managed backups + PITR required because of minors' medical data.
- **Tier B cost ≈ $63/mo** on-demand (VM $25 + Cloud SQL $29 + disk $5 + GCS backups $2 + SES $1 + egress $1). ~$54/mo with 1yr committed-use discount on the VM. Adding FreeScout+Listmonk keeps it within the architecture doc's $45–75 band.
- **Human-gated (automation delivers IaC only, human applies):** live `pulumi up`, DNS registrar delegation, secret values.
- **Cloud Run revisited and DECLINED (2026-08-02).** Scale-to-zero would be ~free for rarely-used request-driven apps, but ungood prioritizes **FreeScout ASAP** — an always-on PHP app (queue worker, cron, inbound email) that doesn't fit scale-to-zero. So keep the single VM. Pool/orchestrator (Nomad) deferred until a 2nd host is genuinely needed.
- **Priority pivot: FreeScout first** (issue #67), ahead of the CRM/Directus and ahead of finishing slice 6. Get a lean working FreeScout on the VM (its own Postgres DB, Caddy TLS, native or Google-OAuth-module login); defer full SSO (#65 oauth2-proxy/LDAP mailbox-mapping) and monitoring (#66) to follow-ups.
- **Dup to consolidate:** slice-6 sub-issue #79 duplicates pre-existing #66 (both "platform backups + monitoring"). Use #66; close #79 as dup.
- **Domains (set from #80 review):** externalDomain (public website) `cyccommunitysailing.org`; internalDomain (admin/staff/volunteer portals) `cycsail.team`; shortDomain (link shortener) `cycsailing.center`. Safe `*.example.com` defaults live in `config.ts`; real values in `Pulumi.prod.yaml`.
- **Pulumi stack renamed `isthmia` → `prod`** (`Pulumi.isthmia.yaml` → `Pulumi.prod.yaml`). Requires `pulumi stack rename isthmia prod` before the next `pulumi up` or state won't carry over.

**DEPLOYED to prod (2026-08-02).** Platform foundation is live: substrate VM (`136.109.86.99`), Cloud SQL `substrate-4aa4a0f` (Postgres 16, db-g1-small, ENTERPRISE edition, private IP), VPC/subnet/firewalls/private-services peering, 3 DNS zones, substrate-runner SA + IAM. DNS zones are inert until the registrar delegates each domain to its NS (external→ns-cloud-e*, internal→ns-cloud-d*, short→ns-cloud-c*, `.googledomains.com.`).

**Deploy gotchas hit (all real, may recur):**
- Bootstrap needs `master@` ADC — `ungood@` lacks project-admin (serviceusage/iam.serviceAccounts.create/etc.); fix tracked in #87 (it-admin Google Group + custom deployer role).
- Long-running podman VM: buildx "Cannot connect to Docker daemon" even when machine shows running → `podman machine stop && start` fixes it.
- Cloud SQL: pin `edition: "ENTERPRISE"` for shared-core `db-g1-small` (new instances default to ENTERPRISE_PLUS which rejects it) — PR #88.
- Cloud SQL create can succeed on GCP but Pulumi's wait errors with an empty `Error waiting for Create Instance:` → instance orphaned (in GCP, not in state); `pulumi import gcp:sql/databaseInstance:DatabaseInstance substrate projects/<proj>/instances/<name>` adopts it cleanly.
- `report-runner-image` has a perpetual `~provider` replace-diff (docker-build provider version not pinned) → rebuilds every deploy; cosmetic, worth a follow-up to pin the provider version.

Decomposition into sub-PRs: (1) auth tooling — folds in #47, PR #72; (2) Pulumi foundation config+secrets; (3) Cloud SQL; (4) networking/TLS/DNS; (5) NixOS VM + deploy; (6) backups+monitoring. Legacy `admin-scripts-runner@` deletion is [[isthmia-cleanup-initiative]] / #58, not this epic.

Revise the design doc at .claude/plans/community-roster.md with the user's answers. These replace the earlier "families first, staff later" decision where they conflict:

1. HOSTNAME: the community site is cycsail.team itself, not my.cycsail.team. Everyone moves onto Authentik now. cycsail.team becomes one Authentik-gated site for staff, volunteers, and families. Staff and volunteer sections are gated by an Authentik group synced from all@, and families' sections by the family group. oauth2-proxy is retired for the portal in this project. Unmatched users still get the help page plus public links. Propose how the staff group gets into Authentik. The obvious option is the same sync job reading all@ membership via the gsuite package's Directory client, but consider Authentik's Google Workspace source if it's simpler, and pick one. Directus staff login can stay on the existing google provider unless moving it is trivially cheap. Say which and why. Update the rollout order so staff lose no access at cutover. For example, stand up Authentik and verify staff sign-in and group gating before switching Caddy. Keep the path/hostname analysis short now that it's one host.
2. MEMBERSHIP: the user chose pure Directus permission filters over materialized roster tables. Drop rosters, roster_entries, and roster_contacts as sync-written tables. Express "teammate" and "contact visible" as live Directus rules. Add whatever alias (o2m) fields on programs and classes are needed, declared correctly by owning package. You may keep a minimal login-to-people mapping if a shared family email truly can't be expressed live. Justify it if you keep it, and prefer live rules keyed on $CURRENT_USER.email if feasible. Mind that Postgres _eq is case-sensitive, so address email normalization. The minor-contact exclusion must still hold. Consider a $NOW-relative date_of_birth filter, with a null DOB treated as a minor. Since the rules can't be tested locally (license), make the production verification plan concrete: a checklist of logins and the expected rows each sees. If some part genuinely can't be expressed in Directus filters, say so plainly as an open question rather than silently materializing it.
3. SEASON: approved as proposed (running, else next, else last), now expressed as a filter if possible. If it can't be a live filter, say so.
4. OPT-IN CONFLICT: the newest answer wins between the portal toggle and the Clubspot field, not portal-always-wins. Design the timestamps needed: when the portal set it, and when the Clubspot answer was given (registration or custom_field_responses time), and where the comparison happens.
5. VM RESIZE: the implementer must stop and report memory numbers before resizing. The user wants to compare the resize against other ways to run containers (e.g. GKE Autopilot) at that point. Do not pre-approve a resize.
6. ADULTS/MINORS: confirmed as proposed.
7. ADDRESSES: send from noreply@cyccommunitysailing.org. The help page points at the main contact inbox (use a <placeholder> if you can't find the address in the repo).

Resolve all old open questions and list only what's still genuinely open. Keep the doc tight, since it's already long, and update Steps accordingly. Report back with a short summary of what changed and any remaining open questions.

308 .claude/plans/community-roster.md
## Approach

`cycsail.team` becomes one Authentik-gated site for staff, volunteers, and families. Authentik
serves at `login.cycsail.team`. oauth2-proxy is retired. `directus.cycsail.team` is unchanged.

### Gating and the portal

Caddy's `cycsail.team` block does four things in order:

1. It strips any client-sent `X-Authentik-*` header.
2. It routes `/outpost.goauthentik.io/*` to Authentik.
3. It runs `forward_auth` against Authentik's embedded outpost, which admits any signed-in user.
4. It serves the portal through Caddy's `templates` handler, for `*.html` files only.

Each section in the page is wrapped in a template condition on the `X-Authentik-Groups` header:

- **Everyone** — the public links, for every signed-in user. Anyone who can prove an email can
  sign in, so these links must hold nothing sensitive.
- **Staff, Volunteers, Instructors** — for the `staff` group, mirrored from `all@`. This matches
  today, where every `all@` member sees every section.
- **Roster** — for the `families` group.
- **Help** — for anyone in neither group. It says to use the email the family registered with in
  Clubspot, or to write to `<contact-inbox>`.

Links for other audiences never leave the server. This settles #98 without an app backend.
`packages/portal` emits the template. Its tests check the rendered conditions, as
`packages/portal/test/render.test.ts` does today.

The roster section is plain ESM from `tsc`, with no bundler. It calls `directus.cycsail.team` with
`credentials: "include"`, and no token reaches JavaScript. The two hosts are the same site, so
Directus's host-only `Lax` session cookie goes with each request. Directus needs
`CORS_ORIGIN=https://cycsail.team`, `CORS_CREDENTIALS=true`, and the portal URL in
`AUTH_AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_ALLOW_LIST`. The page filters by team and school in pure, tested
functions. School grouping uses `normalizeName` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:11`).

### `community-sync`

`packages/community-sync` is a new Cloud Run job with gsuite-sync's plan-and-execute shape. It
depends on `commodore`, `directus`, `gsuite`, `crm`, and `clubspot`. It does not invert the graph.
It has four passes:

- **Login email.** It writes `people.login_email` for every person. The value is `people.email`,
  trimmed and lowercased, or null when `isValidEmail` fails. Move `normalizeEmail` and
  `isValidEmail` from `packages/gsuite-sync/src/membership.ts:34-45` into `crm`, so both syncs
  share one rule. This column is the one login-to-people mapping kept, and only for case. A shared
  email needs no mapping, because `_eq` matches every row that carries it.
- **Season.** It writes `classes.roster_current`. The flag is true when the class's camp is the
  current season for the class's program. The current camp is the one running today, else the next
  upcoming one, else the most recently ended one. A Directus filter cannot pick "the earliest
  upcoming camp", because it cannot compare one row's field with another row's field.
- **Staff group.** It mirrors `all@` into the Authentik group `staff`. It uses `DirectoryClient`,
  with `listMembers` extended to pass `includeDerivedMembership`
  (`packages/gsuite/src/directory.ts:130`). Authentik has no inbound Google Workspace source. Its
  Google Workspace provider pushes the other way.
- **Family group.** It adds every distinct `login_email` of a current participant or their
  guardian to the Authentik group `families`. A config flag keeps this pass off until launch.

The group passes create any missing Authentik user, keyed by lowercased email, before they set
membership. A person's group is then in place at their first sign-in. Both group passes add and
remove members. Unlike gsuite-sync (`membership.ts:121-124`), they are not add-only, because a
stale member keeps access.

`community-sync`'s `schema.yaml` declares `login_email` and `roster_current` as extension fields on
`people` and `classes`.

### Directus schema

- `crm`: `people.share_contact` (nullable boolean) and `people.share_contact_updated_at`
  (timestamp). Null means never answered, and it is treated as not shared.
- `clubspot`: the o2m aliases `programs.classes`, `classes.registration_entries`, and
  `registrations.registration_entries`. `clubspot` owns these relations. `programs.classes` is an
  extension field on a `crm` collection, like `programs.google_group_id`.

### Directus rules

`$ME` stands for `{ "login_email": { "_eq": "$CURRENT_USER.email" } }`. Authentik's scope mapping
for Directus lowercases the `email` claim, so both sides of the comparison are normalized.

- **Acts for (`A`).** `{ "_or": [ $ME, { "my_contacts": { "relationship_type": { "_eq": "guardian" }, "contact_id": $ME } } ] }`
- **Teammate (`T`).** Applied to a person:
  `registration_links.registration_entries` has an entry where all of these hold:
  - `status` is `confirmed`.
  - `class_id.roster_current` is true.
  - `class_id.program_id.classes` has a class with `roster_current` true and a confirmed
    `registration_entries.registration_id.person_id` matching `A`.
- **Adult.** `{ "date_of_birth": { "_lte": "$NOW(-18 years)" } }`. A null date of birth fails
  `_lte`, so it counts as a minor with no special case.

One new role, **Community** (`appAccess: false`), is the default role for the `authentik`
provider, with public registration on. Every rule depends on `$CURRENT_USER.email`, so an unmatched
user reads nothing. The role has three policies, because `DirectusPermissionRule` allows one row per
(policy, collection, action) (`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:199-213`):

| Policy     | `people` action | Fields                                            | Filter                                                                                |
| ---------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `names`    | read            | `id, first_name, last_name, school`               | `T`                                                                                   |
| `contacts` | read            | `id, first_name, last_name, email, phone`         | a guardian of a `T` with `share_contact` true, **or** a `T` that is Adult and opted in |
| `family`   | read, update    | read: `id, first_name, last_name, share_contact` — update: `share_contact` | `my_contacts` has a guardian matching `$ME`, **or** `$ME` and Adult                  |

- The `family` update rule presets `share_contact_updated_at` to `$NOW`. The client can never set
  it.
- The `names` policy also gets read rules on `registration_entries`, `classes`, and `programs`,
  limited to ids and names, so the page can show teams.
- A minor's email and phone are reachable only through `contacts`. `contacts` admits a minor only
  as a guardian's child, and there it returns the guardian's row, not the minor's.
- Directus 11+ returns a policy's fields only for items that match that policy's filter. The
  `names`/`contacts` split depends on this, and the verification below checks it.
- There are no rules on `medical_profiles`, `contacts`, or `registrations` rows themselves.

Two new pieces of infrastructure code:

- `DirectusPolicy`, a resource for an extra policy attached to a role.
- `presets` support on `DirectusPermissionRule`.

The Guardian role stays unused.

**Directus staff move to the `authentik` provider.** Directus usernames are unique emails. A
staff member who is also a parent would collide with the Community user that the `authentik`
provider tries to create, and the Directus login would fail. The move is one change to
`ungoodUser` (`directus-roles.ts:62-68`). `google` stays enabled until that login is verified.
The bootstrap admin password is the break-glass path.

### Opt-in: newest answer wins

`share_contact` sits on the participant row. `promoted_fields` writes the registration's person,
so the Clubspot answer lands there.

- **Portal.** One family toggle updates every participant the viewer is a guardian of. An adult
  participant can also update their own row. The preset stamps `share_contact_updated_at`.
- **Clubspot, from Spring.** The time of an answer is its registration's `registered_at`.
  `custom_field_responses` has no timestamp of its own. `planPromotedFields` gets a newest-wins
  mode for this one target. It writes `share_contact`, and it writes `registered_at` into
  `share_contact_updated_at`, when the winning response is newer than the stored timestamp or the
  stored timestamp is null. It parses Yes and No explicitly, and it counts and logs any other
  answer. `PROMOTABLE_PERSON_FIELDS` (`packages/clubspot/src/promoted-fields.ts:7`) allows text
  only today.
- An answer edited in Clubspot after registration keeps the old `registered_at`, so the sync
  ignores the edit.

### Authentik deployment

- **Containers.** `authentik-server` and `authentik-worker`, with a Caddy block for `login.`. Pin
  a release that needs no Redis.
- **Database.** `postgres.database("authentik")` and a user
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/database.ts:122-141`). `db-g1-small` allows about
  50 connections. Cap Authentik's workers and connection age so that it and Directus fit.
- **Memory.** The VM is `e2-medium` with 4 GB (`compute.ts:11`). Authentik wants about 2 GB. The
  implementer measures `docker stats` and **stops to report the numbers before adding Authentik**.
  The user then compares a resize with other hosting options, such as GKE Autopilot.
- **Secrets.** Pulumi's `randomSecret` in `infrastructure` makes the bootstrap token, the secret
  key, the DB password, and the Directus OIDC client secret. They are granted to `substrate-runner`.
- **Config.** A new Pulumi project, `packages/infrastructure/src/authentik`, applied after
  `infrastructure`. It uses the goauthentik Terraform provider through
  `pulumi package add terraform-provider`, wrapped in classes with secure defaults. It declares:
  - the Google source, with email matching
  - the email-code flow and SMTP
  - the proxy application for `cycsail.team`
  - the Directus OIDC application and its lowercasing scope mapping
  - the `staff` and `families` groups
  - "users cannot change their own email"
  - the sync's service account, whose RBAC role covers creating users and managing those two
    groups only

  It reads the Directus client secret by name, as `crm/index.ts:37-41` reads the admin password.
- **IAM.** The job's service account goes in `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap`, like
  `gsuite-sync.ts`. Its grants go in `config.ts`. It needs domain-wide delegation for
  `admin.directory.group.member.readonly`, which is a manual Workspace step. Its Directus machine
  user gets:
  - read on `people` (`id`, `email`) and update on `people` (`login_email`) only
  - read on `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `camps`, and `programs`
  - read and update on `classes`, where the update is limited to `roster_current`
- **Retire oauth2-proxy.** Remove its container, `portalOauthCookieSecret` (`portal.ts:220-224`),
  and `substrateSelfSign` (`substrate.ts:32-36`). `substrateSelfSign` exists only for oauth2-proxy's
  delegation. Revoke the substrate account's delegation in Workspace.

### Email

Authentik sends as `noreply@cyccommunitysailing.org` through the Workspace SMTP relay. The relay
authenticates the VM's static IP (`compute.ts:24`). Before any code is emailed, fix DNS at the
registrar:

1. Merge the SPF records into one:
   `v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com include:amazonses.com ~all`.
2. Turn on Workspace DKIM, and publish its key.
3. Delete the stray `v=DMARC1` TXT record at the apex. `_dmarc` already holds the real one.

### Production verification

The rules are license-gated, and `dev/directus-local` runs without a license
(`dev/directus-local/docker-compose.yml:10`). They are checked in production against a hidden
Clubspot test camp. Its classes map to test programs P and Q, and one class in P belongs to an
ended camp.

| Login               | Setup                                                                                 |

308 .claude/plans/community-roster.md
## Approach

`cycsail.team` becomes one Authentik-gated site for staff, volunteers, and families. Authentik
serves at `login.cycsail.team`. oauth2-proxy is retired. `directus.cycsail.team` is unchanged.

### Gating and the portal

Caddy's `cycsail.team` block does four things in order:

1. It strips any client-sent `X-Authentik-*` header.
2. It routes `/outpost.goauthentik.io/*` to Authentik.
3. It runs `forward_auth` against Authentik's embedded outpost, which admits any signed-in user.
4. It serves the portal through Caddy's `templates` handler, for `*.html` files only.

Each section in the page is wrapped in a template condition on the `X-Authentik-Groups` header:

- **Everyone** — the public links, for every signed-in user. Anyone who can prove an email can
  sign in, so these links must hold nothing sensitive.
- **Staff, Volunteers, Instructors** — for the `staff` group, mirrored from `all@`. This matches
  today, where every `all@` member sees every section.
- **Roster** — for the `families` group.
- **Help** — for anyone in neither group. It says to use the email the family registered with in
  Clubspot, or to write to `<contact-inbox>`.

Links for other audiences never leave the server. This settles #98 without an app backend.
`packages/portal` emits the template. Its tests check the rendered conditions, as
`packages/portal/test/render.test.ts` does today.

The roster section is plain ESM from `tsc`, with no bundler. It calls `directus.cycsail.team` with
`credentials: "include"`, and no token reaches JavaScript. The two hosts are the same site, so
Directus's host-only `Lax` session cookie goes with each request. Directus needs
`CORS_ORIGIN=https://cycsail.team`, `CORS_CREDENTIALS=true`, and the portal URL in
`AUTH_AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_ALLOW_LIST`. The page filters by team and school in pure, tested
functions. School grouping uses `normalizeName` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:11`).

### `community-sync`

`packages/community-sync` is a new Cloud Run job with gsuite-sync's plan-and-execute shape. It
depends on `commodore`, `directus`, `gsuite`, `crm`, and `clubspot`. It does not invert the graph.
It has four passes:

- **Login email.** It writes `people.login_email` for every person. The value is `people.email`,
  trimmed and lowercased, or null when `isValidEmail` fails. Move `normalizeEmail` and
  `isValidEmail` from `packages/gsuite-sync/src/membership.ts:34-45` into `crm`, so both syncs
  share one rule. This column is the one login-to-people mapping kept, and only for case. A shared
  email needs no mapping, because `_eq` matches every row that carries it.
- **Season.** It writes `classes.roster_current`. The flag is true when the class's camp is the
  current season for the class's program. The current camp is the one running today, else the next
  upcoming one, else the most recently ended one. A Directus filter cannot pick "the earliest
  upcoming camp", because it cannot compare one row's field with another row's field.
- **Staff group.** It mirrors `all@` into the Authentik group `staff`. It uses `DirectoryClient`,
  with `listMembers` extended to pass `includeDerivedMembership`
  (`packages/gsuite/src/directory.ts:130`). Authentik has no inbound Google Workspace source. Its
  Google Workspace provider pushes the other way.
- **Family group.** It adds every distinct `login_email` of a current participant or their
  guardian to the Authentik group `families`. A config flag keeps this pass off until launch.

The group passes create any missing Authentik user, keyed by lowercased email, before they set
membership. A person's group is then in place at their first sign-in. Both group passes add and
remove members. Unlike gsuite-sync (`membership.ts:121-124`), they are not add-only, because a
stale member keeps access.

`community-sync`'s `schema.yaml` declares `login_email` and `roster_current` as extension fields on
`people` and `classes`.

### Directus schema

- `crm`: `people.share_contact` (nullable boolean) and `people.share_contact_updated_at`
  (timestamp). Null means never answered, and it is treated as not shared.
- `clubspot`: the o2m aliases `programs.classes`, `classes.registration_entries`, and
  `registrations.registration_entries`. `clubspot` owns these relations. `programs.classes` is an
  extension field on a `crm` collection, like `programs.google_group_id`.

### Directus rules

`$ME` stands for `{ "login_email": { "_eq": "$CURRENT_USER.email" } }`. Authentik's scope mapping
for Directus lowercases the `email` claim, so both sides of the comparison are normalized.

- **Acts for (`A`).** `{ "_or": [ $ME, { "my_contacts": { "relationship_type": { "_eq": "guardian" }, "contact_id": $ME } } ] }`
- **Teammate (`T`).** Applied to a person:
  `registration_links.registration_entries` has an entry where all of these hold:
  - `status` is `confirmed`.
  - `class_id.roster_current` is true.
  - `class_id.program_id.classes` has a class with `roster_current` true and a confirmed
    `registration_entries.registration_id.person_id` matching `A`.
- **Adult.** `{ "date_of_birth": { "_lte": "$NOW(-18 years)" } }`. A null date of birth fails
  `_lte`, so it counts as a minor with no special case.

One new role, **Community** (`appAccess: false`), is the default role for the `authentik`
provider, with public registration on. Every rule depends on `$CURRENT_USER.email`, so an unmatched
user reads nothing. The role has three policies, because `DirectusPermissionRule` allows one row per
(policy, collection, action) (`packages/infrastructure/src/directus/client.ts:199-213`):

| Policy     | `people` action | Fields                                            | Filter                                                                                |
| ---------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `names`    | read            | `id, first_name, last_name, school`               | `T`                                                                                   |
| `contacts` | read            | `id, first_name, last_name, email, phone`         | a guardian of a `T` with `share_contact` true, **or** a `T` that is Adult and opted in |
| `family`   | read, update    | read: `id, first_name, last_name, share_contact` — update: `share_contact` | `my_contacts` has a guardian matching `$ME`, **or** `$ME` and Adult                  |

- The `family` update rule presets `share_contact_updated_at` to `$NOW`. The client can never set
  it.
- The `names` policy also gets read rules on `registration_entries`, `classes`, and `programs`,
  limited to ids and names, so the page can show teams.
- A minor's email and phone are reachable only through `contacts`. `contacts` admits a minor only
  as a guardian's child, and there it returns the guardian's row, not the minor's.
- Directus 11+ returns a policy's fields only for items that match that policy's filter. The
  `names`/`contacts` split depends on this, and the verification below checks it.
- There are no rules on `medical_profiles`, `contacts`, or `registrations` rows themselves.

Two new pieces of infrastructure code:

- `DirectusPolicy`, a resource for an extra policy attached to a role.
- `presets` support on `DirectusPermissionRule`.

The Guardian role stays unused.

**Directus staff move to the `authentik` provider.** Directus usernames are unique emails. A
staff member who is also a parent would collide with the Community user that the `authentik`
provider tries to create, and the Directus login would fail. The move is one change to
`ungoodUser` (`directus-roles.ts:62-68`). `google` stays enabled until that login is verified.
The bootstrap admin password is the break-glass path.

### Opt-in: newest answer wins

`share_contact` sits on the participant row. `promoted_fields` writes the registration's person,
so the Clubspot answer lands there.

- **Portal.** One family toggle updates every participant the viewer is a guardian of. An adult
  participant can also update their own row. The preset stamps `share_contact_updated_at`.
- **Clubspot, from Spring.** The time of an answer is its registration's `registered_at`.
  `custom_field_responses` has no timestamp of its own. `planPromotedFields` gets a newest-wins
  mode for this one target. It writes `share_contact`, and it writes `registered_at` into
  `share_contact_updated_at`, when the winning response is newer than the stored timestamp or the
  stored timestamp is null. It parses Yes and No explicitly, and it counts and logs any other
  answer. `PROMOTABLE_PERSON_FIELDS` (`packages/clubspot/src/promoted-fields.ts:7`) allows text
  only today.
- An answer edited in Clubspot after registration keeps the old `registered_at`, so the sync
  ignores the edit.

### Authentik deployment

- **Containers.** `authentik-server` and `authentik-worker`, with a Caddy block for `login.`. Pin
  a release that needs no Redis.
- **Database.** `postgres.database("authentik")` and a user
  (`packages/infrastructure/src/infrastructure/database.ts:122-141`). `db-g1-small` allows about
  50 connections. Cap Authentik's workers and connection age so that it and Directus fit.
- **Memory.** The VM is `e2-medium` with 4 GB (`compute.ts:11`). Authentik wants about 2 GB. The
  implementer measures `docker stats` and **stops to report the numbers before adding Authentik**.
  The user then compares a resize with other hosting options, such as GKE Autopilot.
- **Secrets.** Pulumi's `randomSecret` in `infrastructure` makes the bootstrap token, the secret
  key, the DB password, and the Directus OIDC client secret. They are granted to `substrate-runner`.
- **Config.** A new Pulumi project, `packages/infrastructure/src/authentik`, applied after
  `infrastructure`. It uses the goauthentik Terraform provider through
  `pulumi package add terraform-provider`, wrapped in classes with secure defaults. It declares:
  - the Google source, with email matching
  - the email-code flow and SMTP
  - the proxy application for `cycsail.team`
  - the Directus OIDC application and its lowercasing scope mapping
  - the `staff` and `families` groups
  - "users cannot change their own email"
  - the sync's service account, whose RBAC role covers creating users and managing those two
    groups only

  It reads the Directus client secret by name, as `crm/index.ts:37-41` reads the admin password.
- **IAM.** The job's service account goes in `packages/infrastructure/src/bootstrap`, like
  `gsuite-sync.ts`. Its grants go in `config.ts`. It needs domain-wide delegation for
  `admin.directory.group.member.readonly`, which is a manual Workspace step. Its Directus machine
  user gets:
  - read on `people` (`id`, `email`) and update on `people` (`login_email`) only
  - read on `contacts`, `registrations`, `registration_entries`, `camps`, and `programs`
  - read and update on `classes`, where the update is limited to `roster_current`

1. Merge the SPF records into one:

2. Turn on Workspace DKIM, and publish its key.

`AUTH_AUTHENTIK_REDIRECT_ALLOW_LIST`. The page filters by team and school in pure, tested
functions. School grouping uses `normalizeName` (`packages/clubspot-sync/src/people.ts:11`).

### `community-sync`

`packages/community-sync` is a new Cloud Run job with gsuite-sync's plan-and-execute shape. It
depends on `commodore`, `directus`, `gsuite`, `crm`, and `clubspot`. It does not invert the graph.
It has four passes:

- **Login email.** It writes `people.login_email` for every person. The value is `people.email`,
  trimmed and lowercased, or null when `isValidEmail` fails. Move `normalizeEmail` and
  `isValidEmail` from `packages/gsuite-sync/src/membership.ts:34-45` into `crm`, so both syncs
  share one rule. This column is the one login-to-people mapping kept, and only for case. A shared
  email needs no mapping, because `_eq` matches every row that carries it.
- **Season.** It writes `classes.roster_current`. The flag is true when the class's camp is the
  current season for the class's program. The current camp is the one running today, else the next
  upcoming one, else the most recently ended one. A Directus filter cannot pick "the earliest
  upcoming camp", because it cannot compare one row's field with another row's field.
- **Staff group.** It mirrors `all@` into the Authentik group `staff`. It uses `DirectoryClient`,
  with `listMembers` extended to pass `includeDerivedMembership`
  (`packages/gsuite/src/directory.ts:130`). Authentik has no inbound Google Workspace source. Its
### Future work

- Finer staff sections, and roles from #156, replacing the `all@` mirror.
- FreeScout through Authentik's SAML module.

## Alternatives

- **A separate host for families, with oauth2-proxy kept for staff.** The user chose one host.
- **Sync-written roster tables.** The user chose live rules. Only `login_email` and
  `roster_current` are sync-written, for the reasons above.
- **A Postgres generated column for `login_email`.** It is not clear that Directus's schema apply
  creates generated columns.
- **Directus staff stay on `google`.** Rejected, because of the unique email collision.
- **Per-audience static pages, or client-side filtering.** Pages multiply with each group
  combination. Client-side filtering leaves every link in the page source.
- **Authentik blueprints.** Removing an entry does not delete the object, and there is no preview.

## Open questions

1. **The season flag.** The approved season rule cannot be a live filter. Accept
   `classes.roster_current`, written hourly by `community-sync`? The live alternative is a window
   such as "the camp ends today or later". That window merges Fall and Spring while Spring
   registration is open.
2. **A fallback for field scoping.** Suppose production shows that Directus does not scope fields
   per policy, so teammates can read contact fields they should not. Then contact visibility cannot
   be expressed in Directus rules. The fallback would be a sync-written contact collection gated by
   a live `share_contact` rule. Agree to that fallback now, or re-decide then?

## Steps

1. `crm`: add `share_contact` and `share_contact_updated_at`, and move `normalizeEmail` and
   `isValidEmail` from gsuite-sync. Schema change, serialized.
2. `clubspot`: add the three o2m aliases. Serialized.
3. Measure VM memory. **Stop and report the numbers to the user.**
4. DNS: make the SPF, DKIM, and DMARC fixes, and set up the relay. Record them in
   `docs/manual-setup.md`.
5. Infrastructure: the Authentik database, secrets, containers, and the `login.` record and Caddy
   block. `cycsail.team` does not change yet.
6. The `authentik` Pulumi project, added to `just deploy`.
7. `community-sync`: the schema (`login_email`, `roster_current`), the plan functions with tests,
   the executor, the job, the identity, delegation, and the Directus machine user. The family pass
   stays off.
8. Portal and substrate: the templated portal on a temporary `preview.cycsail.team`, gated by
   Authentik. Staff confirm sign-in and the staff sections.
9. Cutover: point `cycsail.team` at the new block. Remove oauth2-proxy, the preview host,
   `portalOauthCookieSecret`, and `substrateSelfSign`, and revoke the old delegation. Staff confirm
   access.
10. Directus: the `authentik` provider, CORS, and `DirectusPolicy` with `presets`. Then the
    Community role and its three policies, and moving `ungoodUser` to `authentik`.
11. Portal: the roster section and the toggle.
12. Run the verification checklist with the test camp.
13. After board approval, turn on the family pass.
14. Spring: the Clubspot opt-in field, with newest wins in `planPromotedFields`.
15. Docs: READMEs, `docs/crm-schema.md`, and the `CLAUDE.md` package list, graph, and auth section.

content.text:
I've committed the approved design doc on the session branch as `5e8dd14a`, with your two changes applied:

- **Season:** a roster now shows every camp running today, meaning today falls between the camp's start and end dates. The hourly flag is gone, and so is the sync step that wrote it. One side effect: between seasons, when no camp is running, rosters are empty.
- **Help page:** it now points at `info@cyccommunitysailing.org`.

I'm holding off on implementation until the one open question is settled. Here's what it's about.

## The contact-fields question

Community users get two separate permission policies on the `people` table:
- **names:** teammates' name and school, for everyone on your team.
- **contacts:** email and phone, but only for guardians of teammates who opted in, and for opted-in adult participants.

The design assumes Directus applies each policy's fields only to the rows that policy allows. So on a minor's row, or a row from a family that didn't opt in, email and phone come back empty.

**The risk:** if Directus instead merges the two policies, granting all fields to any row either policy allows, then every teammate's email and phone would be readable, including minors'. Directus 11's documentation says it scopes fields per row, but that can only be checked on the licensed production instance. The checklist tests it before any family has access, because the family group stays off until board approval.

**The fallback,** if the check fails: families' permissions never include email or phone on `people`. Instead, the sync job writes a separate contacts table holding only guardians and opted-in adults, never minors. A live rule on that table shows only families who opted in.
- **Pro:** minors' contact details never appear in any table families can read, however Directus merges policies.
- **Con:** one more table the sync writes. A changed phone number takes up to an hour to show. Opting in or out still takes effect immediately.

The fallback is safer by construction, so you could also choose it from the start and skip relying on the permission behavior at all.
